explanation: A register dial for everyday, general-audience English about people's practical affairs (homeowners, business owners, renters and landlords, consumer products, sports results, company or committee news, crime and court reports, plain narrative): within such text it builds over the clause and peaks, often above half of max, on the word that links a noun phrase to what comes next (' without', ' with', ' on', ' as', ' unless', a sentence-opening ' On'/' As', or the verb after 'who'/'we', as in 'owners who[ want]'). It stays below about a quarter of max on English technical, scientific, medical, mathematical, academic-research or software-instruction prose (e.g. 'The enzyme catalyzes the hydrolysis...', 'We propose a novel method...', 'To install the package, run...'), on students/essays-type educational text, on non-English text and on short code; long indented code files give only moderate peaks on the whitespace that opens the next statement.
